speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have experienced occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; could you tell me exactly when the surgery was performed and what specific procedure was done?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent Cholesteatoma (likely at the graft site).

The combination of shooting pain when eating (referred pain via the auriculotemporal nerve) and tenderness with earrings (suggesting an anterior or anterior-superior pocket) following a recent tympanoplasty is highly suspicious for a recurrent cholesteatoma. I need to confirm if there is any discharge, foul smell, or changes in hearing since your last audiogram.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent Cholesteatoma.

I have identified the most likely diagnosis based on your surgical history and specific symptoms of referred pain and local tenderness. To confirm this, I require a CT scan of your temporal bone to visualize any bony erosion or soft tissue mass behind your eardrum.
